Hon'Ble Sameer Jain, J.
1 .  Counter affidavit filed by CBI is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Shivam Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Rahul Srivastava, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the CBI.
3.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in FIR No.RC1202024A0008, under Sections 120B and 420 IPC, Section 13(1)(a) Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 and Section 66-C Information and Technology Act, Police Station CBI ACB, Ghaziabad during pendency of the trial.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that as per allegation a Bank Employee Mukul Singh,
the co-accused, fraudulently transferred huge amount of Rs.Four Crore Ninety Eight Lacs from the account of a Company in the account of M/s Star Rays Private Limited and thereafter M/s Star Rays transferred the above amount in the account of five different enterprises including M/s Drishti Traders and Pankaj Tyagi one of the co-accused Proprietor of M/s Drishti Traders gave bearing cheque of Rs.Ten Lacs to one Vinod Kumar Arora and subsequently applicant withdrew this money from the Bank.
He further submits that except this there is no other allegation against the applicant.

5. He further submits that prima facie co-accused Mukul Singh appears to be prime accused and he has already been released on bail by this Court and his bail order has been annexed as Annexure-5 to the affidavit filed in support of the instant bail application.

6. He further submits that co-accused Vinod Kumar was the proprietor of M/s Star Rays in which account entire money of Rs. Four Crore Ninety Eight Lacs were transferred by co-accused Mukul Singh and he has also been released on bail by this Court vide order dated 15.10.2025 passed in Criminal Misc.Application No. 31592 of 2025.
He further submits that the case of applicant is at better footing than co-accused Mukul Singh and Vinod Kumar.
7. He further submits that even entire alleged embezzled amount of Rs.Four Crore Ninety Eight Lacs have already been returned by the Bank in the account of said Company.
8. He further submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history to his credit and he is in jail in the present matter since 25.8.2025, i.e., for almost two and half months.

9. Per contra, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the CBI, however, opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant except the fact that the amount of Rs. Ten Lacs which were withdrawn by the applicant from the Sunil Grover vs Central Bureau Of Investigation And ... on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1134596/

sentences.text: 10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. However, it is a case in which as per allegation by fraudulent means more than Rs.Four Crore Ninety Eight Lacs of a Company were transferred in different accounts but it reflects that this fraud has been committed by co-accused Mukul Singh, the Bank Employee and he has already been released on bail by this Court.
12.

Further, however, as per allegation applicant also withdrew the amount of Rs. Ten Lacs from the Bank but there is no allegation that he committed any misappropriation and only allegation against him is that after receiving a bearer cheque of Rs. Ten Lacs, he withdrew the money.

13. Further, record also suggests that co-accused Vinod Kumar was the proprietor of M/s Star Rays in which account entire money of Rs. Four Crore Ninety Eight Lacs were transferred and he has been released on bail by this Court.
14. Record suggests that case of applicant is on better footing than co-accused Mukul Singh and Vinod Kumar who have already been released on bail.
15. Further, applicant is not having any previous criminal history to his credit and he is in jail since 25.8.2025, i.e., for almost two and half months.

16. Further, law is settled that bail is a rule while bail rejection is an exception and unless proven guilty, an accused is deemed to be innocent and bail application of an accused should not be dismissed either for preventive or punitive purpose.

17. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
18. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

19. Let the applicant-Sunil Grover be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

20. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

21. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
(Sameer Jain,J.) November 7, 2025 SKM
